p: Pattern: an extreme close-up of a soft, fine-textured warm surface filling the crop, centred just beside a dark rounded blob, with small dark ovals nearby and a sharp edge on one side. Examples: the cheek, muzzle side or eye area of a long-furred dog seen very close.
k305: Pattern: smooth hairless skin or fabric seen close, often with a small round dark hole or eye set in it. Examples: a person's shoulders, chest or arms in a vest or T-shirt, people at close range, the eye of a lizard or pufferfish, the round end of a metal tube.
k97: Pattern: a scene with no face at its centre: bodies, backs, legs, clothing or bright objects at mid distance. Examples: an animal's back or harness, a person's torso or raised arm, yarn, a fish, a tricycle. Not: any face, human or animal.
k23: Pattern: dense, busy, high-contrast repeated texture covering the whole crop: many small similar cells, dots, spots or stripes in a regular tiling, with no single central shape. Examples: butterfly wings, keyboards, patterned fabric, spotted fur, lattices.
k297: Pattern: an upright shape: a rounded top patch over a wide flat solid-coloured block filling the lower half. Examples: a person's chin, neck and shirt or jacket front, the chest of an animal seen from the front.
k163: Pattern: bold dark-and-bright patches filling most of the crop, seen close. Examples: a black-and-white dog's face or body, a white blaze between dark eyes, a lamb, a butterfly wing, a glossy dark object with bright highlights (a beetle, a lens, a drum). Not: a whole face seen from a distance.
k275: Pattern: one glossy round eye or lens at the centre, a dark pupil with a bright glint, seen very close. Examples: the eye of a frog, turtle, fish, dog or monkey, a camera lens, a washing machine's round glass door. Not: a whole face, not flat matte discs.
c101: Pattern: a flat area with no central structure: smooth warm reddish or brown surfaces, straight edges or horizontal bands, no ring of fibres and no hub. Examples: wood, cloth, painted walls, furniture, a warm-coloured horizontal patch.
